nodes.title: Positive orbifold Laplacian
nodes.statement: quotientLaplacian Γ is the nonnegative self-adjoint Friedrichs realization of −y²(∂x²+∂y²) on L²(XΓ,μΓ). Start on compactly supported orbifold-smooth functions (smooth invariant lifts at elliptic charts), close their Dirichlet energy q(u,v)=∫⟨∇u,∇v⟩dA, and use the associated operator. nodes.title: Congruence spectral description
nodes.statement: For every allowed Γ, the weight-zero residual L² subspace is exactly the constants. The absolutely continuous spectrum of Δ is [1/4,∞), with one channel per cusp and a scattering matrix. Every spectral value in (0,1/4) is a finite-multiplicity cuspidal eigenvalue; there are finitely many there and no singular continuous contribution. This is an arbitrary-level specialization of AS.4.
hypotheses: Γ≤SL₂(ℤ) contains Γ(N) for some N≥1; its effective image acts on ℍ.
Metric ds²=(dx²+dy²)/y² has curvature −1; all functions are complex-valued.
proofSteps: Import AS.4 spectral orthosum and GL₂ expansion, with the requested multi-cusp scattering and residual classification.

For principal level, diagonalize the finite-level action. Rank-one Eisenstein poles in Re s>1/2 give only the trivial residual character at s=1; the relevant Dirichlet denominators are zero-free in Re(2s)>1.
Pass to Γ-invariants inside the principal-level cover. Retain the channels indexed by Γ cusps and identify the operator on the quotient.
acceptance: Several cusps give several Eisenstein channels, not the level-one single-channel formula.
A positive residual exceptional value must be excluded, not silently treated as cuspidal.

nodes.title: Exceptional cuspidal dictionary
nodes.statement: For allowed Γ and an eigenvalue 0<λ<1/4, a cuspidal GL₂(Aℚ) unitary representation π occurs after passing to principal level and decomposing the finite-level action. Its archimedean component has SO(2)-weight zero and complementary parameter r∈(0,1/2), with λ=1/4−r². A common sign parity on its two real inducing characters is allowed; π∞ need not be O(2)-spherical.

u is a nonzero positive exceptional eigenfunction.
proofSteps: Apply AL.3/global-whittaker-factorization to the cuspidal GLn representation to obtain genericity of every local component before invoking the generic unitary classification. Cuspidality alone is not a definition of genericity.

Use CSG.0 residual classification to identify u as cuspidal. Lift u to Γ(N) and apply AF.2 adelic-classical comparison at principal level, then extract a cuspidal constituent using AF.3/cuspidal-spectrum-discrete, not merely the definition of a cuspidal representation.

Compute the normalized Casimir on the SO(2)-fixed line using AF.1 real local classification. Write the unitary principal-series characters as sgn^ε|.|^r and sgn^ε|.|^−r after the central norm normalization.
Allow both ε=0 and ε=1; the geometric eigenvalue does not force reflection-even parity.
acceptance: Covers Γ(N) and arbitrary intermediate Γ, not only Γ₀(N) with a nebentypus.
Either sign parity yields the same λ.

nodes.title: Monomial archimedean temperance
nodes.statement: If π is unitary cuspidal on GL₂(Aℚ) and has a nontrivial character self-twist, then π=AIK/ℚ(θ) for a quadratic field K and a unitary Hecke character θ. Its archimedean parameter is tempered. Therefore a weight-zero complementary component with 0<r<1/2 has no nontrivial self-twist.
hypotheses: π is unitary cuspidal; there is a character η≠1 with π⊗η≃π.
proofSteps: Import the quadratic self-twist and induction branch of the existing adjoint-lift contract. A global Hecke character’s positive absolute-value part is a common norm power; the central unitarity of its induction forces this power to be zero.
At a split real place induction is the pair of unitary real characters. At a complex place unitary Weil induction is tempered (with the resulting principal/discrete type).
The nonzero real exponents of a complementary weight-zero π∞ contradict temperance.
acceptance: The cuspidal-lift proof cannot be applied to every monomial form.
No complementary r>0 survives this branch.

The resulting spherical component has the required standard gamma factor; central-character removal is essential when ωπ is nontrivial.
